title: Bone graft before dental implants
what: The doctor adds bone graft material where you do not have enough bone for an implant. Over a few months, it grows together with your own bone.
why: When the jawbone has thinned after a tooth was pulled or has been missing for a long time, and there is nothing to hold an implant.
duration: usually 30 minutes to 1.5 hours; healing usually takes several months. Your surgeon will tell you how long
tell_doctor: All your medicines, especially blood thinners. Your doctor will say what to do
Bone-strengthening medicines, now or in the past
If you smoke. It affects healing
Allergies, including to painkillers and antibiotics

prepare.title: Tests
prepare.text: You usually need a 3D scan of your jaw, sometimes blood tests. The clinic will give you a list.

prepare.title: Smoking
prepare.text: Best not to smoke before and after surgery, for as long as your doctor says.

prepare.title: Food
prepare.text: With local anesthesia, you can usually have a light meal beforehand. With sedation or general anesthesia, the clinic will tell you when to stop eating.

prepare.title: After surgery
prepare.text: Have soft, cool food ready at home for a few days.

bring: Someone to take you home, if you have sedation
steps: You sit in the chair, and your mouth is cleaned
You get a numbing shot, and wait for it to work
The surgeon makes a small cut in the gum
The graft material is placed, often covered with a membrane
The doctor gives you instructions and prescriptions for home
feel: During surgery: pressure and vibration, but no pain
Afterward: swelling and aching for a few days. Prescribed medicines help
Sometimes a small bruise on the face
after: Hold something cold to your cheek in the first hours, as your doctor says
Do not rinse hard or touch the stitches with your tongue
Soft food, not hot. Chew on the other side
Stitches usually come out after 1 to 2 weeks
The implant goes in after healing. Your surgeon will say when
red_flags: Bleeding does not stop after pressing gauze firmly for 20 to 30 minutes
Swelling gets worse after day 3, or a fever over 38°C (100.4°F)
Pus, a bad taste, or grains of material coming out of the wound
Trouble breathing or swallowing: call emergency services

faq.q: Can I do without a bone graft?
faq.a: Sometimes a different implant or approach works. The surgeon decides based on your scan.

faq.q: Is it my own bone or artificial?
faq.a: It can be either. Your doctor will explain which material suits you.

faq.q: When can the implant go in?
faq.a: Sometimes right away, but more often after a few months. Your surgeon will say when.

reminders.text: Bone graft tomorrow. Bring your scans and medicine list. Have soft food and an ice pack ready at home.
